name: AnyPS5
description: Tool for automatic PS5 executables porting to Linux and Windows
one_liner: Automatically converts PS5 game programs so they can run natively on a regular Windows or Linux PC, without emulating the PS5 itself.
buyer: Honestly, no one paying for this directly: it's a hobbyist preservation and compatibility-research project, and using it commercially to run paid games without a license is legally murky.
business_use_cases: A game preservation nonprofit documents and verifies which older titles run, for historical and archival purposes.
A hardware reviewer benchmarks GPU performance using open-licensed test titles that run through the project.
An engineer studying console internals uses the relinker and system library implementations as a reference while building their own compatibility tooling.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid consulting to studios trying to understand their own legacy engine's PS5-specific code when porting it to PC.

steal_this: Not really a weekend business. The honest 'steal' is studying its PRX library implementations as a reference while learning low-level porting and compatibility-layer engineering.
